Title: feat(mcp): add Prefab UI for interactive tool responses. Review only this checkout at HEAD. Do not build or run tests. Reply with the full review report.

expected.text: `unwrap_unset` now equates `None` with `UNSET`, silently replacing any legitimate `None` from the API with `default`. For API fields typed `T | None | Unset` where `None` is a meaningful value (e.g., 'explicitly cleared'), callers that supply a non-None default — such as `unwrap_unset(po.order_no, request.order_number)` — will now receive `request.order_number` when the API returns `null`, masking the API's intent. This is a behavioral breaking change to a shared utility.

`create_stock_adjustment` with `confirm=True` directly executes the write without calling `require_confirmation()`, unlike every other write tool in the codebase (`receive_purchase_order`, `fulfill_order`, `create_manufacturing_order`). The field description says 'prompts for confirmation' but the tool will submit destructive stock changes immediately when `confirm=True`, bypassing the user-elicitation step.

`_update_item_impl` performs no API call and returns a success `UpdateItemResponse` when neither item-level nor variant-level fields are set. There is no guard clause that rejects an empty update request. A caller that accidentally omits all fields gets a success response with `name='Unknown'` and a message claiming the item was updated, while nothing actually changed in the API.

This path now depends on the variant cache, but unlike the existing SKU-based item tools (`_search_items_impl` and `_get_variant_details_impl`), it is not wrapped with `@cache_read(EntityType.VARIANT)`. On a cold or stale cache, `check_inventory` will return zero stock for a valid SKU without ever querying the API.

This new SKU lookup has the same cold-cache failure mode: the function reads `services.cache.get_by_sku()` without first syncing the variant cache. A valid SKU can therefore return an empty movement history if variants have not already been cached.

The variant selected by `sku` is not checked against `request.id`/`request.type` before being patched. A request can update item A's item-level fields while also updating the variant for item B if the SKU belongs to another product/material.

This stock adjustment path resolves SKUs from the cache without syncing it first. If the variant cache is empty or stale, preview/creation fails with `SKU not found` for valid items instead of resolving them reliably.

For UI-enabled tools this replaces the previous top-level response dict with the Prefab envelope and nests the actual tool data under `data`, while the non-UI branch still returns model fields at top level. That inconsistent/breaking structured_content shape can break programmatic clients that read fields like `id`, `items`, or `order_number` from the existing top-level response.

The receipt confirm action omits the `items` payload required by `receive_purchase_order` (purchase order row IDs and quantities), and the preview response only stores `items_received`. Clicking this button cannot reliably execute the same receipt with `confirm=true`.

Variant updates now depend on `services.cache.get_by_sku()`, but this implementation is not wrapped with `@cache_read(EntityType.VARIANT)` like the existing SKU-based read tools. On a cold/stale cache, updating valid variant-level fields can fail with `SKU not found`.
